item.title: Sour note: Jazz lose both Lauri Markkanen (wrist) and Jaren Jackson Jr. (knee) in loss to Grizzlies
item.description: Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. both left the Utah Jazz's game against the Memphis Grizzlies on Monday early after suffering injuries in the first half. With the Jazz holding a 13-11 lead midway through the first quarter, Markkanen tried to run his defender, Grizzlies rookie Cam Boozer, off a flare screen from Jackson. Not wanting to get left behind the play, Boozer worked to stay connected to Markkanen through the contact. In the process, Markkanen's right hand got caught between Boozer's arm and Jackson's body, appearing to bend it backward in a fashion that left the 29-year-old Finnish forward in evident pain: Please be ok Lauri🙏🙏🙏🙏🙏 pic.twitter.com/hT1oQ5NZuG — Cap’n Cook 🏔️ (@JazzePinkman) October 27, 2026 Boozer was whistled for a foul on the play. Markkanen promptly subbed out, favoring his right wrist. Shortly thereafter, the Jazz designated him as questionable to return ; about five minutes later, they ruled him out entirely , bringing a premature end to the All-Star forward's night. Markkanen finished with two points in just six minutes of floor time. Not long after Markkanen went to the locker room, Jackson also wound up on the wrong end of a collision when Grizzlies guard Ty Jerome drove to the lane, drew a foul on Jazz defender Svi Mykhailiuk, and fell into the right leg of the stationary Jackson as he stood in the restricted area: Here's the play. https://t.co/zlG2GDWTII pic.twitter.com/I4bdryNrSY — JP Chunga (@JP_Chunga) October 27, 2026 Jackson hit the ground in a lot of pain, and soon joined Markkanen in the locker room, where he too was ruled out for the remainder of the contest . He finished with six points, three rebounds and two assists in 10 minutes, leaving Utah — which is already missing injured center Jusuf Nurkić — without its entire would-be starting frontcourt for the balance of the game. (Nurkić's backup, Jaxson Hayes, also missed the game with right shoulder soreness.) Despite losing two of their three leading scorers on the season, the Jazz persevered. Keyonte George (26 points, six assets), Ace Bailey (17 points, 10 rebounds) and third-string center Mo Bamba (14 points, seven rebounds, four blocks) led a charge that saw Utah whittle what had been a 16-point deficit down to one point with one minute to go in regulation. Jaren Jackson Jr. (second from left) and Lauri Markkanen (third from left) both saw their nights end early against the Grizzlies on Monday. (Rich Storry/Getty Images) Rich Storry via Getty Images The Jazz would never get all the way over the hump, though. Jerome — who entered Monday as the NBA's leading scorer and was just named the Western Conference Player of the Week — scored six of his 15 points in the closing minutes, helping the Grizzlies keep Utah at bay and finish off a 110-105 win to improve to a surprising 4-0 on the young season. Both Markkanen and Jackson will undergo MRI testing on Tuesday to determine the severity of their injuries, Jazz head coach Will Hardy said after the game.

item.title: Brewers’ Sal Frelick lays out for incredible Game 3 catch vs. Rays
item.description: Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Brewers’ Sal Frelick lays out for incredible Game 3 catch vs. Rays appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Milwaukee Brewers are sensing blood in the water, seeing the Tampa Bay Rays on the ropes in Game 3 of the World Series. Even with the Brewers having taken a 10-0 lead in the fifth inning after they scored eight in quick succession, the team wasn’t just about to let their foot off the gas pedal. In fact, right fielder Sal Frelick is still leaving it all on the line to prevent the Rays from getting any traction on offense. With one out in the bottom of the eighth inning, Ben Williamson came to the plate to try and ignite some sort of a rally for the Rays. Williamson then blooped a 1-2 pitch to shallow right, forcing Frelick, who was stationed a bit deep, to scramble forward. He would then have to lay out to make a catch, and the ball nestled into his glove for the second out of the inning. Sal Frelick lays out to make the diving catch! pic.twitter.com/JPGVNlTG7u Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Talkin' Baseball (@TalkinBaseball_) October 27, 2026 On the field is where Frelick butters his bread. The Brewers love him because of his surehandedness in the outfield, and surely enough, even in a game where they’re leading by 10 runs, he’s still willing to hustle and sacrifice his body to get every out he can for his team. Frelick has come up huge already for the Brewers in the World Series. In Game 2, he hit a long ball to tie the game for Milwaukee after they fell behind by four runs in the first inning. Milwaukee would of course go on to win that ballgame, 5-4, setting themselves up nicely with a 2-0 lead in the series heading onto the road. Now, the Brewers are just one win away from breaking through. They took a 10-1 win in Game 3, extending their lead in the series to 3-0. Milwaukee just needs to keep on doing what they’ve been doing — scoring timely runs, nailing down the fundamentals on the field, and executing on the mound — to finally earn their first World Series title in franchise history. item.title: Dante Moore's NFL Draft decision might cost him over $35 million after season-ending injury
item.description: Dante Moore's NFL Draft decision might cost him over $35 million after season-ending injury originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After missing the past three games with a concussion, Oregon Ducks quarterback Dante Moore is not expected to return this season. Dan Lanning explained the situation to reporters during a press conference on Monday. Moore, who was widely projected to be a top pick in the 2026 NFL draft, chose to return to Oregon for his senior year. He was projected to be one of the best quarterbacks in the nation this year and earned preseason Heisman Trophy consideration. The bold move is now more of a huge risk. "If it was up to Dante in any shape, way, he would be out there playing for the guys," Lanning said, adding that Moore has not yet been medically cleared. "This isn't a selfish decision on Dante's part, saying, 'I don't want to come back, the season doesn't look the way I want it to look.' That's not at all what this is." Moore took a vicious hit during Oregon's game against USC on Sept. 26. He attempted to slide after scrambling up the field before he was hit late by linebacker Desman Stephens II. After being down on the field, he was taken to the hospital. Moore sustained a concussion and his scans were clean. So where does this leave Moore in the 2027 NFL Draft? According to ESPN's Mel Kiper Jr., the Ducks QB is No. 25 on the Big Board . If he came out last year and was the No. 1 pick over Indiana's Fernando Mendoza, Moore would have received a 4-year contract worth about $54.4 million . If he's picked when Kiper currently has him in 2027, he'll get $18.7 million. This is a $35.7 million difference. In four games before his injury, Moore had a 69.7% completion rate, 926 passing yards, nine touchdown passes and zero interceptions. "We said before that this is a serious deal that he'll 100% be able to fully recover from. That hasn't changed," Lanning said. "But for him to be out there on the field for us, that's not going to happen. We'd love to have Dante out there, he's still going to be a big part of this team." Oregon has struggled without Moore. Backup QB Dylan Raiola and third-stringer Brock Thomas have both taken turns as the team's starter. Neither ons has been impressive. The Ducks were ranked No. 2 in the AP preseason poll and had national championship aspirations. Now they'll try to figure out how to recover in the second half of the season. item.title: Valkyries’ Veronica Burton makes WNBA Finals history only matched by Diana Taurasi
item.description: Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images Valkyries’ Veronica Burton makes WNBA Finals history only matched by Diana Taurasi appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Veronica Burton pulled off an inspiring effort as she put together a historic performance in the Golden State Valkyries’ 64-55 win over the Atlanta Dream in Game 5 of the 2026 WNBA Finals on Monday night. Burton has been playing in the league since 2022, going through her second season with the Valkyries. She has secured her place as a full-time starter, helping Golden State shine as an incredible squad throughout the campaign. This paved the way for them to make the WNBA Finals for the first time in franchise history. Golden State had its back against the wall with a 2-1 series deficit after losing Game 3. They have since bounced back with wins in Games 4 and 5 to take a 3-2 series lead over Atlanta. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Veronica Burton had a solid night with 13 points, eight rebounds, four blocks, three assists, and one steal. She shot 5-of-15 overall, including 1-of-6 from downtown, and 2-of-3 from the free-throw line. Her efforts placed her in the record books of WNBA Finals history, per the league itself. “Veronica Burton’s four blocks tie Diana Taurasi (2009) as the most blocks by a guard in a WNBA Finals game. Burton also set her postseason career high in blocks,” the post read. How Veronica Burton, Valkyries played against Dream Veronica Burton and the Valkyries are officially one win away from winning the WNBA Finals. They will be in hostile territory in Game 6, but Golden State has serious momentum to make history for the ages. Four players scored in double-digits for Golden State in the Game 5 win, including Burton. Kiah Stokes had a strong night as she finished with 13 points, eight rebounds, three blocks, and one assist. She shot 5-of-6 from the field, including 3-of-4 from beyond the arc. Tiffany Hayes came next with 12 points and three rebounds, Cecilia Zandalasini had 12 points and two assists, while Gabby Williams provided nine points and six rebounds. item.title: Prescott fires Cowboys to 38-21 win over plummeting Eagles
item.description: Dak Prescott of the Dallas Cowboys made 15-of-27 passes with no interceptions or sacks (Mitchell Leff) Dak Prescott passed for three touchdowns and 212 yards as the Dallas Cowboys bounced back with a 38-21 thumping of the injury-ravaged Philadelphia Eagles, who plunged to a fifth straight NFL loss. The Cowboys, whose offense had misfired in back-to-back losses to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Green Bay Packers, pulled emphatically clear of their NFC East rivals in the second half to move to 3-4. CeeDee Lamb made two superb touchdown catches and George Pickens added a third, while the Cowboys also ran for 204 yards spearheaded by Javonte Williams, who had a touchdown and a career-high 155 rushing yards. With their first win in Philadelphia since the 2021 season, Dallas remained in pursuit of the division-leading New York Giants (4-2-1). Meanwhile, the Eagles suffered their fifth straight defeat, having lost starting quarterback Jalen Hurts for the season due to blood clots. The Eagles' woeful injury record worsened as star running back Saquon Barkley, on his return from a two-game absence with a hamstring issue, left the field with a back injury. In an even first half, two excellent catches by Cowboys receivers helped Dallas fight back after the Eagles' rushing game had put Philadelphia ahead twice. After an early Dallas 55-yard field goal, Barkley exploded 29 yards for a first down -- breaking a tackle and then appearing to grab his troublesome hamstring -- but soon after rushed wide to the pylon for an eight-yard TD. The Cowboys hit back. Prescott sent a touchdown pass to Lamb, who took a spinning catch in the far corner of the end zone. In the second quarter, running back Dameon Pierce rushed five yards around the Cowboys defense to put the Eagles back ahead 14-10. On the kickoff return, Tyler Goodson appeared to have done sensationally to run 99 yards for a touchdown, slaloming left and right to avoid tackles, but it was wiped out by a holding penalty. Still, Dallas again responded, going into halftime ahead as Prescott sent a 21-yard corner-pocket TD to Pickens, who managed to tap his toes barely in bounds. After the break, backup Eagles quarterback Tanner McKee found Makai Lemon for the rookie wide receiver's first NFL touchdown to briefly retake the lead. But that was as good as it got for Philadelphia. Prescott launched a second touchdown pass to Lamb, who claimed it over his shoulder, followed by a successful two-point conversion. "That's a guy that gets open, I just have to give him a chance, and he's going to go make the play. And so, credit to him. He makes my job easy," said Prescott, who completed 15-of-27 passes with no interceptions or sacks. Williams rushed into the end zone with barely two minutes remaining to ensure victory. item.title: Red Wings contain Oilers stars as Michal Postava shines in shootout
item.description: Welcome to the NHL, Michal Postava. The Detroit Red Wings goalie (who actually made his league debut in relief last week ) stopped 26 of 28 shots in regulation and overtime in his first career NHL start, as the Wings wrapped up their four-game Western Conference road trip with a 4-3 shootout win at Rogers Place in Edmonton on Monday, Oct. 26. Postava got the Wings to the shootout with a point-blank stop at the top of the crease with just under 7 seconds left in overtime, and then stopped Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl on the first two shots of the skills competiton before stoning Ryan Nugent-Hopkins for the final victory. Lucas Raymond scored the only goal for the Wings in the shootout. SATURDAY NIGHT: Loss to Flames shows how much growth is still needed Michael Postava's third period The 24-year-old Czech goalie entered Monday with a 1.25 goals-against average and .954 save percentage with the Grand Rapids Griffins of the AHL, but gave up a goal on eight shots over 20 minutes against the Vancouver Canucks on Thursday. Against the Oilers, however, Postava kept the Oilers offense tamped down with 11 saves (on 12 shots) through the first two periods. The third was a different story, however, as back-to-back penalties left the Wings on the kill for nearly four minutes. After killing off the first penalty, assessed to Viktor Arvidsson seconds into the third but served by Michael Brandsegg-Nygard, the Wings gave up a goal, by Isaac Howard in a snipe from the left faceoff circle, with 6 seconds left on the second (a trip by Brandsegg-Nygard seconds after leaving the penalty box). The goal was the first of the season for Howard, who won the Hobey Baker Award as college hockey’s best player in 2025 with Michigan State. The Wings knotted it at 2-all just 30 seconds later, as Arvidsson – fresh from getting bloodied during his penalty early in the period, delivered a feed to Emmitt Finnie in front of the net for his fifth goal this season. After a back-and-forth third, the Wings were zapped by a deflection from the left face-off circle by Colton Dach that sent the puck just under the crossbar – but over Postava's left shoulder to break a 2-2 tie. But with Postava sitting on the bench to give the Wings an extra attacker, the Wings tied it again, as Dylan Larkin scored with 77 seconds left, netting his second goal of the season. Detroit Red Wings playoff position The overtime loss kept the Wings (4-4-4) hovering just above the Eastern Conference cellar, with 12 points. item.title: ‘Read the room’ – NFL fans are divided after CeeDee Lamb mocked Eagles after Cowboys win
item.description: Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images Dallas Cowboys star CeeDee Lamb didn’t miss a chance to take a shot at the Philadelphia Eagles after their MNF win, and NFL fans can’t agree on whether it was okay. It is a tough time to be a fan of the Philadelphia Eagles. The team fell to a 2-5 record after their latest loss against their division rivals, the Dallas Cowboys. Things are likely to only get worse from here too, with star quarterback Jalen Hurts set to miss at least the entirety of this season with his health issues. For the Cowboys, this was a much-needed win against a fierce rival. They have struggled in the last few weeks, losing winnable games and failing to get the job done. So it would make sense that getting this win resulted in some extra celebration from their stars. However, CeeDee Lamb’s particular choice of celebration is causing some debate online. CeeDee Lamb was mocking the ‘Fly, Eagles, Fly’ celebration on the field and some fans think it wasn’t a classy move All sports have certain unwritten rules and expectations that the players are expected to follow. When to celebrate, how to celebrate, how much to celebrate, all fall into this category. However, not everyone agrees on these and a fair few people don’t even subscribe to the notion. Dallas beating an extremely injured Philly side ideally shouldn’t warrant too much celebration, but that doesn’t take into account their rivalry. So when CeeDee mocked the team with a ‘Fly, Eagles, Fly’ celebration of his own, it caused some debate online. “CeeDee Lamb mocks the Eagles as he walks onto the field after the Cowboys win. Extremely disrespectful,” one fan wrote. “Cowboys beating the eagles 4th and 5th string team is their Super Bowl. Classless,” another said. “Frontrunning when we don’t have Hurts. Read the room,” a third fan wrote. “It’s absolutely impossible to be disrespectful to an Eagles fan,” a fourth fan commented, sharing the opposite view. “There is absolutely nothing bad about that at all,” another claimed. “Nah! Everyone knows Philly fans are the worst. It’s nice to see them get what they give,” a sixth fan said. Whether Lamb was right to do what he did or not is a matter of personal opinion for every fan. Some are going to love it, and some will think that it is uncalled for. What remains unchanged is the result. As of Monday, the Cowboys have earned the right to celebrate, whatever the circumstances may be. This is basic football knowledge yet coach Brian Schottenheimer has gotten away from it situationally throughout the year and outright altogether last week. item.title: Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d’Or as England captain beats Yamal and Mbappe to top prize
item.description: After a night of delays, confusion and a long, long wait, Harry Kane finally strode on to the stage at the London Palladium at 10.51pm to receive the Ballon d’Or. It has been 12 years since Kane burst into the national consciousness as an unassuming 21-year-old with an eye for goal. The extraordinary, self-willed career that followed may not have delivered the most coveted team trophies, but as Kane turned the golden orb in his fingers, he finally held football’s ultimate individual crown. Kane is only the fifth Englishman to win the prize after Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Michael Owen. It is 25 years since Owen’s award and 70 years since Matthews won the inaugural Ballon d’Or, the serendipitous anniversary that brought this ceremony from Paris to Kane’s hometown. It had been a tense wait over recent weeks as 100 journalists around the world decided the best player of the 2025/26 season. Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal turned on the PR campaigns in an effort to woo swing voters: Mbappe played to the African bloc while Yamal tried to directly undermine Kane’s candidacy, hinting he lacked the “magic” of a true winner. On the night there was some controversy too, when the Ballon d’Or’s official website published separate articles proclaiming all three favourites had won, hours before the ceremony began. Someone at head office presumably had a heart attack and swiftly deleted them, but not before the internet had screenshotted receipts. Outside the Palladium there was chaos, as every surrounding street was choked with people poking phones over security barriers to get a digital glimpse of their favourite players. Inside the theatre, an announcement was made of a half-an-hour delay which turned into an hour. A Frenchman named Charlie came out to pump up the audience, calling for “massive energy tonight”, like a beleaguered manager talking to a dressing room he’d long since lost. When the show finally began, Spain’s Alexia Putellas won her third Ballon d’Or, and Bukayo Saka was recognised for his charity work. Yamal was named the world’s best young player, but he finished behind Kane for the main men’s prize. item.title: Mbappe dropped by Chinese brands for 'offending national sentiments'
item.description: France and Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe arrives at the Ballon d'Or in London (FRANCK FIFE) Kylian Mbappe was dropped Tuesday by two major brands in China after a video circulated online in which the French football star apparently joked about former leader Mao Zedong. In China jokes about Mao, the country's founding leader who died in 1976, are considered disrespectful and remain a social taboo. "Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments," drinks giant Dongpeng said in a statement, adding that "with immediate effect we are terminating all cooperation with Kylian Mbappe". Mengniu, China's largest dairy producer, also cut ties with the Real Madrid and France forward. "With immediate effect our company is terminating all cooperation with Kylian Mbappe," Mengniu said in a statement. "Mengniu firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any words or actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people," it added. The announcements came after a video emerged online with Mbappe saying that the funniest internet meme he had seen was of his face photoshopped onto that of "some guy -- I think he's a Chinese dictator". This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappe superimposed on an image of Mao, one of several using the footballer's face and other historical figures. The authenticity of the video could not immediately be verified by AFP Fact Check. "Dongpeng Beverage ends cooperation with Mbappe" was the top-trending topic on Chinese social media site Weibo. One Weibo user said that the "extremely serious wrong remarks... crossed the red line. They are completely unacceptable". Others urged Dongpeng to remove Mbappe's image from their energy drink bottles. Dongqiudi, one of China's biggest online football outlets, said in a statement on Monday evening that Mbappe’s remarks were "offensive to China and the Chinese people" and "have hurt the feelings of Chinese football fans and the Chinese people". Mbappe addressed the memes depicting him as historical figures, including strongmen leaders, in an interview with French sports newspaper L'Equipe in September. "There's a part of it that's funny. item.description: Milwaukee's Robert Gasser threw six shutout innings while allowing only one hit and facing the minimum 18 batters as the Brewers routed Tampa Bay 10-1 in game three of the World Series (ELSA) With a devastating 16-hit batting performance and masterful pitching by Robert Gasser, the Milwaukee Brewers routed Tampa Bay 10-1 on Monday, reaching the brink of a World Series sweep. Left-handed starter Gasser threw six shutout innings, allowing only one hit with a walk and three strikeouts in facing the minimum 18 batters. "It was awesome," Gasser said. "We're going to enjoy tonight. It was a great team win. But we've got work to do." Jackson Chourio, a 22-year-old Venezuelan outfielder, went 4-for-5 at the plate, scored twice, stole a base and also drove in a run in the Brewers' historic eight-run fifth inning to humble the Rays. All eight runs came with two outs in the inning, a World Series record, and Milwaukee batters made seven consecutive hits, a playoff first. "It was special for sure," Chourio said through a translator. "We've been preparing for this day. We've known it was coming. We have one more to lock in for tomorrow to complete the mission." The Brewers seized a 3-0 lead in Major League Baseball's best-of-seven final and can win the first title in team history with a triumph in game four on Tuesday at Tropicana Field. "There's still one more game to go for us to win," Gasser said. "I know everybody is eager to do it and we're going to show up tomorrow ready to go." Gasser became the first lefty to face the minimum over six innings in a World Series clash since Sandy Koufax of the Los Angeles Dodgers in 1965. The Rays managed a run in the ninth but only three hits in the game. Chourio raced home from second base on a Christian Yelich single in the third inning to score the first run and William Contreras drove in another with a hit to right field for a 2-0 lead. The Brewers, whose only prior World Series was a 1982 loss to St. Louis in seven games, had two one-run wins to start the Series but overwhelmed Tampa Bay with a barrage in the fifth. Chourio singled, stole second and advanced to third on a Contreras single that loaded the bases as Rays starter Freddy Peralta, who had played for Milwaukee the past eight seasons, was lifted for relief pitcher Cam Booser. Brice Turang followed with a two-run single up the middle, Garrett Mitchell added a single to score Contreras, and Cooper Pratt followed with a two-run double to left field for a 7-0 Brewers lead.
